verdict.rationale: CRA documents a sanctioned system-to-system channel, EFILE. Developers certify their tax software with CRA, and enrolled electronic filers transmit client returns directly from that software, using an EFILE number and password to maintain the account and view transmission history. The step-by-step enrollment application itself is only asserted in a supplementary summary, not quoted from first-party pages, and the evidence covers only T1 filing, not batch, payroll or business-program transmission. missing for 10: verbatim first-party enrollment/application steps for EFILE, evidence of transmitter/batch channels beyond T1 individual returns (e.g., payroll or business program transmission), independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a legal-ops lead, a documented system-to-system channel exists for software to transact with the service (system accounts, transmitter programs, batch providers), with the enrollment path published

citations.quote: electronically file their clients' current and first seven prior years' income tax and benefit return information to the Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) directly from their EFILE–certified tax preparation software

the developer of the tax preparation software has gone through a process with the Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) to verify that their product is compatible with the CRA EFILE electronic tax filing service.
Use your EFILE number and password to: Maintain your account, Renew your account, View transmission history
certified software plus an enrolled electronic filer transmit returns system-to-system, with the enrollment path published on the agency's own pages.
